requirements.requirement: Locate sternum medially, axilla laterally and an intramammary node within breast tissue in the regional schematic.
Locate axillary levels relative to pectoralis minor: I lateral, II behind/between its borders and III medial/infraclavicular, rather than sequential disease stages.
Branching drainage and illustrative node locations do not assign an individual sentinel map, sampled status or tumour involvement; mapping and examination are distinct claims.

An in-situ component within an intact duct boundary can coexist with a separate invasive component in surrounding stroma at one time; no inevitable transition or hole in this particular intact duct is asserted.
Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

In the selected cartoon, the stromal invasive component lacks an enclosing intact duct rim. This is not a universal stain rule, marker test or diagnosis; real invasion assessment needs tissue morphology and appropriate supporting tests.

Chosen cell shapes, colours and counts in the coexistence scene are schematic, not measured proportions, grade, stage, stain, prognosis or a patient diagnosis; no metastatic or inevitable progression arrow is implied.
IDC/NST identifies a histologic category rather than an ancestral larger-duct cell; type, grade, receptors and stage require distinct evidence.
Local stromal invasion and distant spread are different claims; two spatial comparison scenes do not establish chronology or systemic spread.
One illustrative TDLU comprises a terminal duct and its associated hollow acini connected toward a larger duct; the larger duct is outside the grouping.
Stroma lies around and between ducts/acini. A TDLU grouping bracket is an annotation, not a shared capsule or basement-membrane envelope enclosing all acini.

In the simplified normal acinus, the lumen is inside luminal epithelium, then living myoepithelium, then extracellular basement membrane, with surrounding stroma; each duct/acinus retains its own boundary.
A magnified acinar cutaway is one acinus, not the entire breast, lobule or TDLU; a magnification inset or bracket is not added tissue.
The normal anatomy scene has no universal acinus/cell count and does not establish cancer ancestry, milk flow, invasion, metastasis, an assay result or a treatment decision.

scienceVersusConvention: Anatomical claims, illustrative geometry and custody/execution claims remain distinct.
